/itineraryStops/2/description.source_en:
Bukchon ('Northern Village') is a 600-year-old hanok (traditional Korean tile-roofed house) residential district nestled between Gyeongbokgung and Changdeokgung Palaces — historically home to high-ranking Joseon Dynasty officials and aristocrats — and today Seoul's largest concentration of preserved hanok homes (~900 traditional houses). 

The signature route walks the **Bukchon 8 Gyeong (8 Famous Views)** with the iconic #6 viewpoint at Gye-dong-gil framing cascading hanok rooftops with N Seoul Tower in the distance — Seoul's most-photographed traditional architecture scene. Bukchon is a LIVING village (not a museum) — residents have publicly requested respectful behavior including quiet hours and limited photography of doorways. 

From Bukchon's southern edge, **⟦G1⟧** (인사동) — Seoul's premier traditional crafts and cultural street — is a 5-10 minute walk. ⟦G1⟧ combines the 4-story spiral **Ssamzigil** complex (70+ craft shops, galleries, cafes, rooftop terrace), traditional teahouses (Mokyeon, Suyeonsanbang), hanji (mulberry paper) workshops, ceramic galleries showing Goryeo celadon and Joseon white porcelain, and Korean souvenir vendors. 

Pedestrian-only on weekends (Sat-Sun). Your driver-guide's flexibility lets you spend more time wherever the group's interest pulls — Bukchon photography vs. ⟦G1⟧ shopping is a natural in-the-moment choice. 

The village's preservation is overseen by **Jongno-gu District Office's ⟦G0⟧ preservation program** — strict zoning rules limit commercial signage, renovation must use traditional materials (handmade hanji paper screens, wooden frames, tile roofs), and the Red Zone entry restriction from 17:00 to 10:00 is enforced by signage and community wardens during peak season.
